en:
Hello, everyone. Nice to meet you.
My name is Tomoharu Hosoda.
I'm in Class 2-C.
Still, this really is a big school, isn't it?
There are seven of us gathered here, and I don't recognize a single face.
Forget knowing anyone, I've never even seen any of you before.
...Sorry, that was a rude thing to say.
It'd be nice if we could use this chance to become friends.
So, it's {a}{f:|}, right?
Since we're here, I thought I'd tell you a story that'll do you some good.{p}Do you know which place at school, besides the classroom, people go in and out of the most?
I know
I don't know
I see. You're a sharp one, just as I thought.{p}
So, where is it?
The faculty room
The restroom
The club room
The school gate

Holding it in is bad for your body, whoever you are.
So during the few hours you spend at school, you're bound to go to the restroom a few times.{p}

{f:You always go too|That's just normal}, {f:don't you|isn't it}?
Everyone relies on the school restrooms.
But as far as I know, there was just one person who never used the school restrooms.
It wasn't that he was constipated, or had some strange illness.
No matter what happened, he never, ever went to the toilet.
In other words, he didn't excrete.
Can you believe a person like that exists?
Well, there is one.
His name was Kiyoshi Takeuchi.
He was a third-year when I was a first-year, so he was two years older than me.
So, when you hear about someone who's never once gone to the toilet, don't you picture some huge fatso?
But no, he was skin and bones.
Like a piece of wire.{p}

{f:Well, naturally|I don't know if you're one of them, though}.
I think a lot of women are romantics who dream about how wonderful it'd be if they never had to go to the toilet.
Girls determined to uncover Takeuchi's secret were always stalking him, their eyes glittering.
Anyone who didn't know would've thought he was a real ladies' man.
Seriously, I hear a TV station even asked to interview him.
Apparently Takeuchi flatly refused, though.{p}
But still, you can't believe there's a person who never excretes, can you?
I can believe it
I can't believe it
Maybe someone like that could exist

Right?
I think you're right.
In the end, nobody really believed it either, whatever they said.
Deep down, everyone thought he must be sneaking off to the toilet when no one was looking.
Or else that maybe he was just someone who needed to go abnormally rarely.
As for me, honestly, I just thought Takeuchi was pretty amazing, and I wasn't interested in him beyond that.
I never really wished I didn't have to go to the toilet, or even thought about it.
If anything, I liked that unique feeling of release you get in the toilet.
Maybe I just lack delicacy?
So I knew about Takeuchi, but it was all one-sided; he didn't even know I existed.
There was no way our paths would ever cross.
But then.
One day, believe it or not, Takeuchi came up and talked to me.
I was totally shocked.{p}

I was eating lunch in the cafeteria when all of a sudden he said,
"Hey, is the seat next to you free?"
and sat right down without waiting.
I mean, Takeuchi was famous at school, and he was my senior, right?
On top of that, we'd never met.
My heart was pounding.
"Ah, y-yes, it's free, sir,"
I said, all tense.
But Takeuchi turned out to be a pretty easygoing guy.
He was always smiling, and he was easy to talk to.
Takeuchi had a big tray with three plates of curry rice and a large bowl of udon on it.
I figured someone must be joining him, but right before my eyes he polished off the whole lot.
I eat a fair amount myself, but that surprised me.
Even after he finished, he looked totally unfazed, without a flicker on his face.
They say skinny people are the biggest eaters, and it's true.
I stared hard at Takeuchi's body, wondering where in that frame all that food could go.
He ate all that, and he still never went to the toilet, right?
I was strangely impressed.
He must have noticed the way I was acting.
"It's strange that I eat so much, isn't it?"
he suddenly said.
I just scratched my head and kept bowing.
"Uh-huh,"
or,
"Well..."
I dodged it with vague things like that.{p}

And that was the end of it that day.
I forgot all about it after that.
Or rather, I didn't really think anything of it.
Takeuchi had just happened to sit next to me; it wasn't as if he'd wanted to talk to me.
He seemed to chat with anyone in a friendly way, so he'd casually talked to me too, since I happened to be next to him. That's what I figured.
Anyone would think that, right?
But then.
It didn't stop at that one time.
The second time, we happened to pass each other in the hallway.
Takeuchi had a crowd of girls trailing after him, as usual.{p}

"Hey!"
he called out, greeting me.
I was startled.
I was impressed he even remembered the face of someone who'd just happened to sit next to him in the cafeteria.
I hurriedly greeted him back, but Takeuchi just kept smiling like always and walked off.{p}

Not that I'm the starstruck type, or into guys or anything.
But it still gets your heart pounding.
Getting to know someone famous, I mean.
It was around then.
That I started to really notice Takeuchi.
I got it into my head that maybe he wanted to be friends with me.
I had no grounds at all for thinking he'd want to be friends with someone like me.
It was just a feeling.
Even so, I didn't have the nerve to talk to him first, and it'd be embarrassing if I'd got it wrong, right?
So I only imagined it and never acted on it.
And then the third incident happened.{p}

It was on my way home from school.
I was trudging along when I heard someone calling me from behind.{p}

I turned around in surprise, and there was Takeuchi, running toward me and waving.
I looked around.
He had to be waving at someone other than me, I thought.
But there was nobody around except me.
No matter how I looked at it, he was waving at me.
While I was thinking all that, Takeuchi was suddenly right beside me.{p}

"Man, those girls are relentless.
It was a real pain shaking them off.
They won't get anything good out of hanging around someone like me,"
he said, laughing as he caught his breath.
As usual, I just grinned awkwardly and kept bowing.
Maybe I'm just bad with people.
"You're Hosoda, right?"
That shocked me.
Takeuchi actually knew my name.
When I just stared blankly, he burst out laughing.
"What are you so surprised about?
Is it really that surprising?
It's not strange that I'd know who you are, is it?"
He said that like it was nothing.
From where I stood, it was more than strange enough.
I couldn't even begin to guess how he knew about someone like me.{p}

I didn't know what to talk about.
I was nervous, you see.
Takeuchi talked to me about all sorts of things, but, pathetically, I don't remember much of it.
And I couldn't give him any decent answers.{p}

"Hosoda, are you free today?"
He asked me that out of the blue.
I was thrown.
While I was fumbling for words,
"If you're free, why don't you come over to my place?"
he even asked.
Why would Takeuchi invite me to his house? The mystery only got deeper.
No matter how I thought about it, I couldn't find a reason.
Why me?
Why would he need to invite someone like me to his home?
Maybe there was no need to think so hard about it, but that's just how I am.
I can't help thinking about things.
I didn't know how to answer him.{p}Takeuchi seemed to be waiting for my answer...
Say you'll come
Say you'll politely decline
Say you have plans today and ask him to make it another day

There was no reason to say no.
Besides, I couldn't believe Takeuchi was a bad person.
I didn't know why he was inviting me, but I answered,
"Ah, I'd be honored to come."{p}

I hadn't known this, you see.
Takeuchi's father was an airline pilot.
And his mother was apparently a famous writer of poetry and essays.
Unfortunately, I didn't know her name.
It was like a picture-perfect family, right?
The kind ordinary people can't understand, I guess.
You can't really picture it, can you?
And their house was huge, too.
I guess that's what you'd call a palace.
I stopped in front of the gate and couldn't move for a while.
Someone like that inviting me? It just got stranger and stranger, right?
I followed Takeuchi, pretty much doing whatever he told me.{p}

The inside was amazing too.
Maybe that's what hotels abroad are like?
Well, I've never seen one, so I wouldn't know.
"Make yourself at home.
You don't have to tiptoe around me.
Don't hold back, okay?"
He said it with a laugh, but... easier said than done.
We lived in completely different worlds.
Everything I saw and touched was new to me.{p}

Before long I was shown to Takeuchi's room.
It's embarrassing to say, but I felt like Takeuchi's room alone was about as big as my whole house.
Maybe that's an exaggeration, but that's how big it felt.
"Want something to drink?"
Takeuchi asked me as I gawked around the room.{p}What should I do?
Coffee
Juice
Tea
Nothing, thanks

"...Ah, I'm fine, thanks."
I quickly bowed my head.
"I told you not to hold back.
...I know.
I've got an interesting drink.
My dad picked it up when he went to India.
It's called Sanbura tea, and once you drink it, you get hooked.
Let's have some of that."{p}

Takeuchi was really kind.
After a while, this Sanbura tea, as he called it, was set down in front of me.{p}

It was pitch black, more like coffee than tea.
It had a bitter, grassy smell, like medicinal herbs.
"It has an unusual taste, so people either love it or hate it, but once you get used to it, it's irresistible.
Go on, try it."
That's what he said, pressing it on me.{p}Would you drink it, if it were you?
Drink it
Don't drink it

"...Uh.
Thank you."
I just thanked him and didn't reach for it.
It might have been rude not to drink it, but something unknown like that is scary, after all.
Takeuchi didn't push it any further, either.
A long time passed after that, but my nerves didn't ease at all.
If anything, the more time passed, the tenser I got.{p}

"You've heard the rumor about me, haven't you, Hosoda?"
Takeuchi said that out of nowhere.
If it was a rumor, there was only one it could be.
I nodded silently.
"To tell you the truth...
That rumor is true.
I've never gone to the toilet.
Because I don't need to."
When someone says something like it's the most natural thing in the world, you end up oddly convinced.
Somehow, it started to seem natural to me, too.
Even so, Takeuchi and I were different.
Maybe because we were talking about it, I suddenly needed to go to the toilet.
"...Um.
Where's the toilet?"
That's when Takeuchi gave a strange laugh.
"The toilet, huh? There isn't one in this house.
Nobody who lives here ever goes to the toilet.
Sorry.
...If you can't hold it, you should drink that tea."{p}

Then he jerked his chin toward the Sanbura tea.
No toilet in the house?
Can you believe that?
What's more, he was saying it wasn't just Takeuchi who never went; it was everyone in the house.
I was so shocked I couldn't speak.
"That tea is really good for your health.
It removes all the impurities from your body.
It turns what would normally become waste into sweat, and pushes it out through every pore of your body.
So no matter how much you eat, you never get fat.
And it's good for you, too.
Isn't that wonderful?"
That's what he started saying.
What would you do?{p}Should I try drinking the tea?
Drink it
Don't drink it
Even so, I didn't drink it.{p}

Takeuchi edged closer to me.
His face was still smiling, but there was something really frightening about him.
"Come on, there's no need to be shy.
Drink that tea and right away you won't need to go to the toilet anymore.
And it changes your body's whole constitution. It's amazing.
It feels fantastic.
Come on, just humor me and drink it."{p}

I saw it.
Under the skin of Takeuchi's cheek, tiny green things were squirming around.
Like the microorganisms you see when you look through a microscope.
You'd never notice unless you looked really close.
Maybe Takeuchi read the look on my face.
"There's nothing to be afraid of.
These are a kind of plant.
They become active once they get inside a human body.
Just like animals.
And they eat up all the impurities for you.
So there's nothing to be afraid of.
It's not scary at all."
As he said it, Takeuchi's eyes were not those of a normal person.
And then I saw it.{p}

"...It might itch a little at first.
They're active under the skin, you see.
When they chew through your blood vessels and race all through your body with your blood, you might feel a little nauseous.
But hey, that's only at first.
You'll get used to it soon.
The important thing is getting used to drinking it.
After that, you'll feel refreshed."
As he said that, Takeuchi pinned my body down.
And then he forced the Sanbura tea down my throat.{p}

"Ugh!"
I spat it out on reflex.
How foul it was... I can't even put it into words.
Like crushing an insect between your teeth and using your tongue to spread the juices that ooze out of it all over your mouth...
The taste must have been something close to that.
In exchange for never having to go to the toilet, you stop being human.
You become a human-plant hybrid.
No, maybe drinking that tea lets the plants take you over.{p}

Takeuchi breathed his grassy breath on me.
"I have a feeling you and I could be good friends.
Right, Hosoda?"
As he said it, his mouth opened wide.{p}

The inside of his mouth was completely covered in earth-colored plant vines, or roots, or something like that.
They had dug into the flesh of his mouth, and they were twitching and quivering.{p}

And from deep in his throat, a grublike creature thickly covered in something like moss was peeking out.
Was it a plant, an animal, or an insect...?{p}

"Aaagh!"
I shoved Takeuchi away and ran out of the house as fast as I could.
Even after I got home, I was shaking all over for a while.
Worst of all, for two or three days that taste wouldn't leave my mouth.
I couldn't eat anything.
Whatever I ate, that taste would spread through my whole mouth...
I stayed home from school for several days, too.{p}

When I finally felt better and went to school, I heard Takeuchi had suddenly transferred.
I didn't tell anyone that I'd gone to Takeuchi's house, or about what happened there.
Even if I told people what I went through, nobody would believe me anyway.
Today is the first time I've ever told this story.
{a}{f:|}.
If you'd been in my place back then, what would you have done?
Would you stop being human in exchange for a comfortable body?
If someone somewhere ever offers you some mysterious tea, I think you'd better not touch it.
There are still lots of things in this world that people like us can't understand.{p}

...To tell you the truth, I'm looking for that Sanbura tea right now.
I went to Takeuchi's house, but they'd already moved out, so I can't get any from him...
Lately, I keep strangely remembering what Takeuchi said back then: that once you drink it, you get used to it.
It tastes awful, but sometimes you want to taste something like that again anyway.
No, for some reason, I feel like this time I could actually enjoy it.{p}

And, it's probably just my imagination, but lately my body's been strangely itchy.
It feels like something's under my skin, and I can't stand it.
I spat it out right away back then, but maybe, without realizing it, I swallowed a little of the Sanbura tea.
And maybe, over all these years, it's been settling into my body.{p}

...I'm sure it's just my imagination.
Here, take a look inside my mouth.
You don't see anything weird, do you?
...It's okay.
I'm still human.
But, {a}{f:|}.
If you ever hear any rumors about Sanbura tea somewhere, be sure to tell me.
Please, I'm begging you.
That's the end of my story, but... you promise, right, {a}{f:|}?{p}

The club room, huh...
Well, clubs are certainly big at this school.
I can see why you'd think that.
But I was hoping for a different answer.{p}

I think people go in and out of the restroom more.
I mean, girls often go to the restroom together with their friends, right?
Several times a day, even.
And guys, if they're at school for hours, will use the restroom a few times too.
So it's the restroom after all.{p}

Huh? You can believe it?
What I can't believe is someone like you.{p}

Ah, no, sorry.
Did that offend you?
I didn't mean anything by it, so forgive me.
Ah, I see.
You're someone with an honest heart who believes anything.
That's rare these days.
But I'd like you to hold on to that heart forever, I really would.
Oh, sorry.
I got a little off track there.
In my case, at first I couldn't believe that Takeuchi never went to the toilet.
But I found out it seemed to be true.
At a school with this many students, going to the toilet without anyone ever seeing you is next to impossible.
Even so, I wasn't as interested in Takeuchi as the people around me were.
Though I was jealous that he was always surrounded by girls.{p}

Sure, Takeuchi was a good-looking guy.
He was captain of the soccer club, and its ace striker.
He had a clean-cut face, and he really did look like he'd be popular with girls.
But still, he wasn't so good-looking that he should have had that many girls hanging on him. If anything, he was the kind of guy you'd find at any school.
With a face like that, he got that popular just from not going to the toilet.
If I just held it in at school, I think I could have even more girls hanging on me than Takeuchi did.
You think so too, right?
.................
Well, never mind.
Let's go on with the story.{p}

Actually, I tried it myself.
Not going to the toilet at school, I mean.
But I couldn't do it.
Sure, for two or three days I can tough it out somehow.
But you have to keep it up until the people around you notice.
There's no way I could keep it up that long.
I was really impressed by how amazing Takeuchi was.
And then I discovered that Takeuchi had an interesting hobby.{p}

One day, a teacher asked me to run an errand over to the old school building.
Normally I make absolutely sure I never go near a place that creepy.
That day, the weather was really beautiful.
Even the old school building, which always has such an eerie air about it, felt different from usual: bright and clear.
I walked past the side of the old school building and around to the back of it.{p}

Then I noticed a boy in uniform standing there all alone, looking up at the sky.
It made me jump.
I mean, I never thought there'd be anyone in a place like that.
I thought a ghost had appeared or something.
The old school building is that kind of place, you know.
It wouldn't be strange for one to show up even in broad daylight.
But when I looked more closely, the person was Takeuchi.{p}

Takeuchi noticed me and kept staring my way.
I gave him a little bow and walked over to him.
I didn't have any business with him, but once our eyes had met, I couldn't just ignore him.
"Hello."
I greeted him.
"Hey."
Takeuchi answered briefly.
"What are you doing in a place like this?"
I asked him.
I mean, he was standing somewhere people don't normally go.
You'd be curious what he was doing, right?
Takeuchi answered.
"...I'm sunbathing.
What about you? What are you doing in a place like this?"
"A teacher asked me to, um..."{p}

Takeuchi said,
"I see,"
and looked up at the sky again.
"Can you see something up there?"
I said, and I looked up at the sky too.{p}

The clouds were drifting slowly by, and it made me feel really good.
"There's nothing to see...
I just like being here like this.
Nobody's ever here, so I can relax and look at the sky like this."
"Is that right?
Well then, I'll hurry up and finish my errand and go, so take your time."
With that, I left.{p}

Because Takeuchi didn't seem to like me being there.
I thought Takeuchi was a strange one.
Sunbathing all alone at lunch break: don't you think that's strange?
Normally you'd be playing soccer in the schoolyard, or chatting with your friends in the classroom, right?
I got interested in Takeuchi, and I thought I'd like to talk to him again.{p}So I...
Went to Takeuchi's classroom
Went behind the old school building

But Takeuchi wasn't there.
I went over to where he'd been standing and looked all around, but there wasn't a soul in sight.
I'd just assumed Takeuchi was always here on sunny days.
So I was a little disappointed.{p}

After that, I went to that spot every sunny day.
But Takeuchi never showed up.{p}And so I...
Went to Takeuchi's classroom
Went behind the old school building

I did wonder if Takeuchi had stopped coming here.
But I figured I'd run into him sooner or later, so I kept going to that spot every lunch break.
Even so, Takeuchi never showed up.
And while I kept at it, I noticed a little something.{p}

It had been bugging me for a while: there was some kind of plant I'd never seen before growing in that spot.
It seemed to me that it was in a slightly different position from the day before.
I thought maybe I was imagining it, but I couldn't stop thinking about it.
So I marked the spot where the plant was, and went back to the classroom for the day.
The next day.
I went to that spot to check the mark.
And sure enough, its position was slightly off from the mark I'd made on the ground.
I thought that was weird.
Something that shouldn't be able to move was moving, after all.
I decided to check one more time, so I made another mark and started heading back to the classroom.{p}

It happened when I'd come around to the front of the old school building.
I heard a voice behind me calling out to me, so I turned around.{p}

And there stood Takeuchi.
"Oh, Takeuchi. Hello."
"Hey, long time no see."
Takeuchi came over to me.
"Huh, I just went to the spot where you were before, but you weren't there, were you?"
I asked him.
"Yeah, I know.
I was a little way off.
More to the point, it looks like you've been coming there every day lately too."
That was Takeuchi's answer.
"Wait, you've been coming there every day too?
I never saw you at all..."
"That's right.
I was a little way off."
That made me go, huh?{p}

That spot has a pretty clear view, and there's hardly anywhere to hide, so where could Takeuchi have been that I never noticed him?
But there was something that bothered me even more, so I asked Takeuchi about it.
About that strange plant.
He'd been going there longer than I had, so I figured there was no way he didn't know about it.{p}

"Takeuchi, do you know about the strange plant growing where I first met you?
That plant always seems to be moving a little, somehow."
Takeuchi looked startled, and answered.
"I know.
You mean that weird plant, right?
What about it?"
"That plant is in a slightly different place every day, or something... Haven't you noticed, Takeuchi?"
Takeuchi's face suddenly turned serious, and he said:{p}

"I never asked your name..."
"Oh, sorry.
I'm Tomoharu Hosoda, Class 1-C."
"...Hosoda.
I like being alone in that spot.
Because you come every day, I can't enjoy my breaks anymore.
...I know perfectly well I'm being selfish.
If you don't have any business there, I'd like you to stop coming..."
With that, Takeuchi walked off in a hurry.{p}

What a selfish guy, right?
Even I, as easygoing as I usually am, got a little ticked off.
But somehow I had a feeling Takeuchi was hiding something.
Maybe it was about that plant.
Takeuchi knew something about that plant, and he was hiding it.
And he didn't want me finding out, so maybe that's why he told me not to come there.
That's what I thought.{p}And so I...
Turned right back to investigate
The next day, went behind the old school building earlier than usual
The next day, went behind the old school building as usual

The next day, curious about what Takeuchi was hiding, I went behind the old school building earlier than usual.
If I got to that spot before Takeuchi and hid, I might be able to learn his secret.
That's what I thought.
I skipped lunch, raced down the stairs, and ran all the way to that spot.{p}
When I reached the side of the old school building, I peeked around just in case, to see whether Takeuchi had come yet.{p}

(Oh no. Takeuchi's already here...)
That's right, Takeuchi had gotten to the spot before me.
The third-years' classrooms are on the first floor, so it's no surprise he got there first.
I watched him for a while, careful not to be seen.
Takeuchi was looking up at the sky, just like the first time I met him.{p}

I looked up too, but I couldn't see anything except thin, slowly drifting clouds.
Takeuchi stayed like that for a while.
As I kept watching, Takeuchi started glancing around, as if to make sure nobody was nearby.
I kept watching him, careful not to be spotted.
Then Takeuchi raised both hands and held them up to the sun.
After checking his surroundings once more, Takeuchi stretched his body up, as if standing on tiptoe.
(Ah!)
I swallowed the cry that nearly escaped my mouth.{p}

Takeuchi's body began to turn green, little by little.
I couldn't believe my eyes.
Something like plant sprouts came out of both his arms.
As if I were watching footage on TV, the sprouts shot out with a rustling swish, stretched out in an instant, and unfurled big leaves.{p}

I got scared and tried to run away.
The moment I turned around and tried to take a step...
I tripped.
The moment I tried to lift my foot, I couldn't step forward, as if something had grabbed hold of it.
I looked down at my feet, and I was shocked.{p}

Something like plant roots, stretching up from the ground, had wrapped around them.
While I frantically tried to tear them off, I looked over at Takeuchi.{p}

I thought these root-like things wrapped around my feet had to be coming out of Takeuchi's feet.
I desperately tried to tear them off.
I was so scared.
But it was no use.
No matter how hard I pulled, instead of breaking, they just dug deeper into my legs.
Wincing in pain, I screamed,
"Takeuchi!
I won't tell anyone about this, so let me go!"
That's what I screamed.
Even so, he wouldn't let go of my legs.{p}

When Takeuchi pointed both hands at me, a bunch of vine-like things began growing out of them, stretching toward me.
The coiling, twisting vines started wrapping themselves around my body.
It was so disgusting, so scary...
I finally broke down crying.
"I'm sorry, I'm sorry!
Forgive me. Please forgive me!
Let go, let me gooooo!"
Even so, he wouldn't let go.
The vines wrapped around me dragged me along, pulling me closer to Takeuchi.
I fought back desperately, but I couldn't move at all.
In the end, I was dragged right up next to Takeuchi.{p}

When I opened my eyes a crack, Takeuchi's face was right in front of me.
There were lots of lines like leaf veins running across it, and I couldn't bear to look.
As I tried to look away, Takeuchi followed and peered into my face.
The vines grabbed my head and forced it to turn toward him.
Takeuchi's face loomed right in front of mine.
Then, letting out a rustling hiss, he spoke to me.
The grassy breath hitting my face was so disgusting I couldn't stand it.
"Hosoda. You've seen my secret...
But that's all right.
I'll make you one of us too.
That way, nobody will ever give the secret away."
With that, Takeuchi opened his mouth wide.{p}

Inside Takeuchi's mouth grew something like roots, joining his upper and lower jaws.
Parting those roots, something like the tip of a stalk, covered in lots of little red beads, came stretching out.
It looked like a horsetail shoot with salmon roe stuck into its tip.
The red beads were slimy, and really disgusting.
And it was trying to force its way into my mouth.
I kept my mouth clamped shut with all my might.
The red beads pressed against my lips.
It felt just like having seedless grapes pushed against them.
I resisted desperately, but the vines squeezed me so tight that my mouth came open.{p}

It came into my mouth.
It kept coming and coming, all the way down into my stomach.
And it moved around as if it were churning up my stomach.
More than painful, it was just so disgusting.
Maybe I passed out. I don't remember anything after that.
But I clearly remember how disgusting it felt.{p}

..................
When I came to, I was lying there on the ground.{p}

Takeuchi was already gone.
When I remembered what had happened, I felt sick.
...I threw up.
And mixed in with it were the red beads from the tip of that stalk.
Thinking those beads had been inside my body made me feel sick all over again.
